documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Cardiology / Cardiac Intensive Care Unit. DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 05/01/2026)

Patient: Anjali Rahman, 55F, DOB 05/03/1970. Admitted Sunday 04/26/2026 to the CICU via the ED. Transferred to cardiac step-down floor 04/28/2026. Discharged home 04/30/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute pulmonary edema with atrial fibrillation and rapid ventricular response.
Background: severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, chronic heart failure (NYHA III), pulmonary hypertension secondary to valve disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, rheumatic fever in childhood.

Presentation: sudden onset of shortness of breath and palpitations early on 04/26 with cough productive of pink, frothy sputum. BP 130/80, HR 120 irregularly irregular, T 36.9, SpO2 89% on room air. Bibasilar crackles. Apical diastolic rumble with an opening snap after S2.
Chest x-ray: pulmonary edema, enlarged left atrium. ECG: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, no ST changes.
Labs: INR 2.4 on arrival. hs-troponin I 4 ng/L (normal). K 4.3, Cr 0.88. Hgb 12.8. Repeat 04/29: K 4.4, Cr 0.97.

Course: Treated with supplemental oxygen, IV furosemide, and IV metoprolol followed by oral metoprolol. Warfarin continued at her home dose; INR remained therapeutic. On hospital day 2 she converted to sinus rhythm on telemetry and oxygen was weaned to room air. Moved to the cardiac floor 04/28. By discharge breathing at her baseline, SpO2 97% on room air, HR 70 in sinus rhythm, BP 118/74.

Discharge medications (home regimen, unchanged):
- warfarin 5 mg PO every evening, target INR 2-3
- furosemide 40 mg PO daily
- metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg PO daily
- potassium chloride ER 20 mEq PO daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: primary care within one week with INR and basic metabolic panel. Cardiology follow-up advised. Return for recurrent breathlessness, palpitations, bleeding or chest pain.

Attending cardiologist, Cardiac Intensive Care Unit

documents.title: In hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted to tell you I have been in the hospital since Sunday. My breathing became very bad suddenly and I was coughing pink foam. They gave me oxygen and IV medicine, my heart is back to normal rhythm. Today they moved me out of the ICU. They say maybe home Thursday.

documents.title: RE: In hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, I'm glad you're out of the ICU. When you get home, call the office and we'll see you early next week and check your INR and blood work. Ask them to send us the discharge paperwork.

documents.body: Discharge summary received. Called pt, home since 4/30. Breathing "back to my usual." No palpitations. Taking warfarin 5, furosemide 40, metoprolol succinate 50, KCl 20 - same as before the hospital, no new prescriptions. Weight this morning 64 kg. Visit with PCP Tues 5/5 at 10:00 with INR and BMP. Pt asked for a note for work, will bring the form.

S: Home 5 days. Breathing is back to where it was before: walking on the flat fine, stairs slow her, two to three pillows as before. No pink sputum since the hospital. No palpitations. Weights 63.5-64 kg. Taking all meds. No bleeding. Off work since the admission.

O: BP 114/83, HR 77 regular, SpO2 96% RA, wt 63.9 kg.
Comfortable, speaking easily. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm, apical diastolic rumble. No JVD. No edema.

Med rec: warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily. Matches discharge list.

A/P:
1. Acute pulmonary edema with AF/RVR, resolved. Back to her usual exertional limit.
2. PAF, in sinus. Continue metoprolol succinate 50.
3. Warfarin: INR today.
4. Severe rheumatic MS, chronic HF NYHA III, pulmonary HTN: continue furosemide 40/KCl 20. BMP today. Low salt, daily weights; call for weight up 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week, any pink or bloody sputum, palpitations.

5. Work note given: may return 5/6.
RTC 3 months.

CARDIOLOGY CLINIC NOTE (received 05/20/2026)
Re: Anjali Rahman, DOB 05/03/1970. Visit 05/18/2026, follow-up after hospital admission.

Interval history: admitted 04/26-04/30/2026 with acute pulmonary edema and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; back in sinus rhythm on day 2 and home on her usual regimen. Since then her breathing is back to its usual limit: fine on the flat, slowed by stairs, two to three pillows at night. No palpitations, no further pink or bloody sputum, no chest pain.

Current medicines: warfarin 5 mg nightly (target INR 2-3); furosemide 40 mg each morning; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once a day; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once a day. NKDA.

Examination: BP 116/76, heart rate 70 and regular, SpO2 97% on room air. Lungs clear. Apical diastolic rumble with her turned onto her left side. No ankle edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm with left atrial enlargement.

Assessment: severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, symptomatic, with chronic heart failure NYHA class III, pulmonary hypertension secondary to the valve, and a recent admission for pulmonary edema; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, in sinus today, anticoagulated. The valve needs to be opened. Percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy is the first choice if the anatomy is suitable and there is no clot in the left atrium.

Plan:
- Transesophageal echocardiogram at the regional hospital echo lab to assess the valve and exclude left atrial thrombus. She stays on warfarin for it.
- Referred to the structural heart team for commissurotomy.
- Medications unchanged. INR monitoring continues with primary care.

Attending cardiologist

events.reason: Transesophageal echocardiogram before mitral balloon commissurotomy

documents.title: Transesophageal Echocardiogram Report
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
TRANSESOPHAGEAL ECHOCARDIOGRAM (received 06/05/2026)
Regional hospital echocardiography laboratory. Study 06/03/2026.
Indication: severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, assessment before percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy.
Procedure: moderate sedation and topical pharyngeal anesthesia; probe passed without difficulty. On warfarin. Rhythm sinus, heart rate 66.

Findings:
- Left atrium enlarged. No thrombus in the left atrium or left atrial appendage.
- Mitral valve rheumatic, leaflets thickened with fusion of both commissures. Wilkins score 8: mobility 2, thickening 2, calcification 2, subvalvular thickening 2.
- Mitral valve area 1.1 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 10 mmHg at a heart rate of 66. Trivial mitral regurgitation.
- Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, ejection fraction 60%.
- Aortic valve normal.
No complications. Discharged home after recovery from sedation.

Conclusion: severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, valve area 1.1 cm2, Wilkins score 8, trivial mitral regurgitation, no left atrial thrombus. Anatomy suitable for balloon commissurotomy.

Echocardiography attending

documents.title: Structural Heart Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
STRUCTURAL HEART CLINIC NOTE (received 06/05/2026)
Re: Anjali Rahman, DOB 05/03/1970. Seen 06/03/2026 after her transesophageal echo, on referral from her cardiologist.

Severe symptomatic rheumatic mitral stenosis with chronic heart failure NYHA class III, pulmonary hypertension secondary to the valve, and an admission for pulmonary edema in April. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, in sinus rhythm today.
TEE today: mitral valve area 1.1 cm2, mean gradient 10 mmHg, Wilkins score 8, trivial mitral regurgitation, no left atrial or appendage thrombus.

Current medicines: warfarin 5 mg nightly (target INR 2-3); furosemide 40 mg each morning; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once a day; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once a day. NKDA.

Recommendation: percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy. We discussed the expected benefit, surgical valve replacement as the alternative, and the risks, including bleeding, tamponade, stroke and worsened mitral regurgitation that could need surgery. She wishes to proceed.

Booked: Tuesday 06/16/2026, regional hospital cardiac catheterization laboratory, one night in hospital.

Warfarin: last dose the evening of Thursday 06/11. No bridging. INR checked on arrival the morning of 06/16 and must be under 1.5 to proceed. Restart warfarin 5 mg the evening of the procedure, then INR with primary care on 06/23.
Continue furosemide, metoprolol succinate and potassium chloride, including the morning of the procedure.

Structural heart cardiologist

reports.text:
Transthoracic echocardiogram, regional hospital, the morning after percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy.
Mitral valve: thickened rheumatic leaflets with improved opening. Mitral valve area 1.9 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 4 mmHg. Mild mitral regurgitation.
Left atrium enlarged. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, ejection fraction 60%. No pericardial effusion.
Rhythm during study: sinus.
reports.conclusion: After balloon commissurotomy: mitral valve area 1.9 cm2, mean gradient 4 mmHg, mild mitral regurgitation, no pericardial effusion.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Cardiology. DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 06/18/2026)

Patient: Anjali Rahman, 56F, DOB 05/03/1970. Admitted electively 06/16/2026. Discharged home 06/17/2026.

Procedure: percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy, 06/16/2026, structural heart cardiologist.
Indication: severe symptomatic rheumatic mitral stenosis (valve area 1.1 cm2 by TEE 06/03, Wilkins score 8) with pulmonary hypertension secondary to the valve and an admission for pulmonary edema in April 2026.
Background: chronic heart failure (NYHA III), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, rheumatic fever in childhood.

Pre-procedure: warfarin held after the evening dose of 06/11. INR 1.3 on arrival. Sinus rhythm.
Procedure: right femoral venous access, transseptal puncture, intravenous heparin during the case, Inoue balloon dilation of the mitral valve. Mean transmitral gradient 10 mmHg before, 4 mmHg after. No complications.
Echo 06/17: mitral valve area 1.9 cm2, mean gradient 4 mmHg, mild mitral regurgitation, no pericardial effusion, LV ejection fraction 60%.
Course: groin site dry, no hematoma. Sinus rhythm throughout on telemetry. Walking the ward without difficulty.

Discharge medications (home regimen, unchanged):
- warfarin 5 mg PO every evening, target INR 2-3 (restarted the evening of 06/16)
- furosemide 40 mg PO daily
- metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg PO daily
- potassium chloride ER 20 mEq PO daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: INR with primary care 06/23. Cardiology clinic with echocardiogram in about six weeks. No heavy lifting for one week. Return for bleeding or swelling at the groin, sudden breathlessness, palpitations, chest pain, or weakness or trouble speaking.

Structural heart cardiologist

reports.text:
Transthoracic echocardiogram, cardiology office, six weeks after percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy.
Mitral valve: thickened rheumatic leaflets with improved opening. Mitral valve area 1.9 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 4 mmHg. Mild mitral regurgitation.
Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 35 mmHg.
Left atrium enlarged. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, normal systolic function. Aortic valve normal. No pericardial effusion.
Rhythm during study: sinus.
reports.conclusion: Mitral valve area 1.9 cm2 after commissurotomy, mean gradient 4 mmHg, mild mitral regurgitation; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 35 mmHg.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CLINIC NOTE (received 07/31/2026)
Re: Anjali Rahman, DOB 05/03/1970. Visit 07/28/2026, six weeks after percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (06/16/2026).

Interval history: breathing easier since the procedure. Stairs still slow her, but she no longer has to stop partway up a flight. Sleeps on two pillows and has not woken breathless since. No palpitations, no blood in sputum, no chest pain. Groin healed. Back on warfarin with INR in range.

Current medicines: warfarin 5 mg nightly (target INR 2-3); furosemide 40 mg each morning; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once a day; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once a day. NKDA.

Examination: BP 118/74, heart rate 68 and regular, SpO2 98% on room air. Lungs clear. Softer apical diastolic rumble. Right groin healed. No ankle edema.

Echocardiogram today: mitral valve area 1.9 cm2, mean gradient 4 mmHg, mild mitral regurgitation, estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 35 mmHg; left atrium enlarged; left ventricle normal in size and function.

Assessment: rheumatic mitral stenosis after successful balloon commissurotomy, result holding at six weeks; chronic heart failure NYHA class III, symptoms improved; pulmonary hypertension secondary to the valve, estimated pressure lower; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, in sinus, anticoagulated.

Plan:
- Medications unchanged. Warfarin continues indefinitely, target INR 2-3, monitored by primary care.
- Transthoracic echocardiogram yearly, sooner if symptoms return.
- Cardiology clinic in six months, January 2027.

Attending cardiologist
